chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Bishr ibn Salama, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever gives charity when he enters the morning, Allah will remove from him the inauspiciousness of that day.

key_terms.الصدقة: Sadaqa — voluntary charity or alms given for God's sake; distinct from obligatory zakat
key_terms.النحس: Nahs — inauspiciousness, ill omen, or misfortune associated with a given day or time
key_terms.يُصبح: Yusbihu — to enter the morning, to wake at dawn and begin the day

ai.seo_question: Does giving charity in the morning remove misfortune according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that giving sadaqa (voluntary charity) at the beginning of the day is a means of warding off misfortune and ill omens. This hadith reflects the early Islamic understanding that charitable acts have a protective spiritual function, connected to the concept that good deeds deflect harm and that God rewards generosity by averting calamity. The teaching encouraged the faithful to begin each day with a charitable act as a form of spiritual armor.
word_analysis: he wakes up in the morning/enters morning

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Bishr Bin Salma, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who gives charity when he wakes up in the morning, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Remove from the inauspiciousness (troubles) of that day’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Bishr ibn Safmah from Misma’ ibn ‘Abd af-Mafik who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
If one gives charity in the morning, Allah removes ill-omened matters from him.’”
